correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the coset condition to determinant one and a trace identity. The nonzero-trace case forces a common nilpotent line. In the traceless case, the pairwise product condition produces a nondegenerate alternating form on a two-dimensional trace-orthogonal plane, forcing all traceless parts onto one line. Determinant-one elements of the resulting quadratic algebra have exactly 2q, q-1, or q+1 elements. Equality and its converse are explicit. Exhaustive exact checks for q=3 and q=5 agree.

value.rationale: For finite subgroups the motivating virtual-solvability theorem is quantitatively vacuous. The new result gives a natural complete two-dimensional finite-field rigidity theorem: abelianness, a sharp order bound, a three-type quadratic-algebra classification, and exact equality cases. This directly clarifies the finite-field boundary of the new coset theorem.
